Bolters are the standard-issue weapons of Warhammer 40,000 s Space Marines, and they fire bolts. But they re not just bolts not really. As befitting the grim darkness of 40K s far future, the bullets that Space Marines fire are individual rocket-propelled grenades, each backloaded with enough fuel to force them through ceramite armor, and frontloaded with enough explosive to shred the soft meat hidden inside that armour. notes.title: Space Hulk: Deathwing Enhanced Edition is out now
notes.content:
Space Hulk: Deathwing must have been a dream project for little French indie studio Streum On, creators of the endearingly janky E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy. As a team they’d started their careers with making Warhammer 40,000-themed mods, so having the official key to the kingdom must have felt like a miracle, but with a famous license and a higher budget comes higher expectations.

While undoubtedly more polished than E.Y.E, Deathwing still felt like a low-budget game with a high-budget facade. After an additional year and a half of development and launching alongside the PS4 version of the game, an Enhanced Edition rolled out today, addressing many of the flaws of the original launch and for those with the original version, it’s a free upgrade.

notes.title: How the Enhanced Edition fixes Space Hulk: Deathwing
notes.content:
Back in 2011, French indie studio Streum On released E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy, an atmospheric shooter/RPG that took a fair bit of inspiration from Warhammer 40,000 and collected a cult following in spite of its bugginess and oddity. When Streum On announced they were doing a legit 40K game it seemed like a perfect follow-up—they were obviously fans of the setting, and this time they might make something a little more polished.

They sort of did. Space Hulk: Deathwing took a board game that had been the inspiration for four other videogames and did something different with it, turning it into a first-person shooter whose main strength was atmosphere. The space hulks of the title are ships lost between dimensions that drift back into realspace merged together, engine rooms connecting to gothic cathedral interiors full of aliens called Genestealers with the wrong number of arms. Leading a squad of Space Marines into a hulk in Deathwing was eerie. Inhuman cries echoed down the corridors and mechanical servo-skulls hovered around scanning everything.

Although Deathwing turned out OK, it felt a bit confused about what it wanted to be, with a co-op mode that required you either start earning abilities from scratch every session or play in the "codex mode" that gave you all of them, with nothing in between. It also had a framerate that dropped whenever swarms of enemies were on the screen—and for a game all about clearing swarms of enemies, that was a problem.

But Streum On have been tweaking and patching away and now are unveiling their Enhanced Edition of Deathwing. It's been optimized hugely, and I only encountered one framerate drop in hours of play. The multiplayer's been revamped, with a system for leveling up and a suite of persistent customization options. There are new enemies and weapons. It's almost but not quite a whole new game.

The customization's worth elaborating on. One of the things about Deathwing that pleased 40K fans was how it got the look of the Space Marines right, their bulky terminator armor covered in chapter insignia and other ornate cruft. There's now even more variety to it, including hyper-detailed banners. There's an extra class too, the Chaplain, who wears a skull-mask, carries an electric sceptre, and looks like the Archbishop of Badass. Some of the equipment and perks you can buy has minor effects like reducing cooldowns by 10%, but they're unlikely to be game-changing and you remain pretty fearsome from level one. 

In the story mode you don't get to see this because you're stuck playing the protagonist, but each level you finish gets added to the list of replayable Special Missions. These you can jump into with a custom Marine whether solo or co-op, returning to maps with a huge number of randomized objectives—repetition is one of the things the original was criticized for and this is obviously a way of dealing with that.

No matter which mode you play you'll also get to face new enemies, like the bio-blast strain who detonate when they die and brutish hybrid aberrants who look like ogres carrying mining equipment. But while the Marines look exactly like they should, the Genestealers have a lumpiness that makes them a bit less threatening than they should be, like they're bubbly from spending too long in the oven.

Shooting remains a bit off too, with the guns having lots of muzzle-flash and recoil (a surprising amount given they're in the hands of walking tanks), but little impact. Melee weapons are whiffy too, and make me miss the meaty hand-to-hand of Vermintide. These are issues that seem too deeply embedded to be entirely remedied by the other enhancements. Similarly, the squad AI still feels dopey—part of the problem there is that their barks trigger at daft times, and they'll do things like warn you about "the claws of xenos approaching" even while surrounded by a mob of the things.

Deathwing remains a game for the 40K hardcore, who will lap up the environments and spend hours earning renown points to buy the sweet Guardian of the Covenant outfits. The improved framerate and some fresh blood in the multiplayer will give fans an excuse to jump back in and shout about PURGING FOR THE EMPEROR once again, but it's still tough to recommend to anyone else. Still, within its niche it does the job, and it's an entirely free upgrade for those who own the original. Which is nice.

notes.title: Space Hulk: Deathwing becomes Enhanced in May
notes.content: Polish your crotchskull and prepare to demonstrate renewed devotion to the Emperor, as Space Hulk: Deathwing will officially become the Enhanced Edition on May 22nd. This is the last in a series of free updates intended to expand and improve the squad-based FPS, which had the looks of Warhammer 40K but didn’t have the touch. It was too janky and just too thin, which is a shame because it has such lovely Gothic spaceships and such big crotchskulls. Fingers crossed this update can find that magic. Not that I believe in magic; that would be heresy. Ah yes, I love the Emperor, I surely do. (more…)

In order to help us to locate and fix bugs, please include the dump files and DxDiag in your report. Try to give us as much details as possible about the issue and what you were doing when it happened. Screenshots are also welcome.
[list]
[*]Dump files - first, you must enable the visibility of “Hidden Folders” in your Windows settings. You can find how to do it on Google. Then, go to "C:\Users\CURRENTUSER\AppData\Local\SpaceHulkGame\Saved\Logs" (replace "currentuser" by your User Name on your computer). If you crashed, the game automatically creates a folder that you can compress into a .zip (or .rar) file and attach in your post.
[*]DxDiag - Press the WINDOWS key (bottom left), then type DXDIAG in the Search Bar and click on the corresponding program. A diagnosis will be executed then. After it's done, click on "Save all information" and save the DxDiag as text file (.txt).
After this, all you need to do is to compress them into a zip file (with the Dump files) and attach it to your post here with a detailed description of your crash.
[/list]

[b]The Emperor calls once again for your assistance - to battle!

The Deathwing Team[/b]

With only one month left until Space Hulk: Deathwing's release, you can now [b]watch 17 minutes of uncut gameplay from the solo campaign.[/b] Clocking at around 15 hours of gameplay - more if players take time to explore, finding hidden relics on the way - the campaign boasts huge environments, with a wealth of optional areas and secret rooms to discover.

Space Hulk: Deathwing's extensive solo campaign is written in collaboration with Black Library author and Dark Angels specialist, Gav Thorpe, as well as cooperative multiplayer. 

The solo campaign sees you playing as a Librarian of the Dark Angels' 1st Company, the Deathwing, taking on swarms of Genestealers in the Space Hulk Olethros with Storm Bolter and Force Sword in hand. The Librarian is a Psyker, granting him access to powerful psychic abilities such as chain lighting, a powerful lightning bolt, which arcs between multiple enemies; and Shockwave, which blasts enemies back from you. 

You will need to utilize the full armory of the Deathwing company, your powerful psychic abilities, as well as the squad members under your command to fend off the xenos threat. 

The Genestealers adapt their behaviour, based on their numbers, their type, and your actions. Commanding your teammates to cover you, block doors to prevent genestealers from flanking you, heal you, or hold a key position, is vital to survival in the depths of the Space Hulk. 

By playing the campaign you'll also unlock new weapons for use by you and your squad mates, along with gaining experience to spend on three skill trees to unlock powerful new abilities.

notes.title: For The Lion!
notes.content:
[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/46/1479396432-shd-gif-1.gif[/img]

Greetings Librarians!

The release of Space Hulk: Deathwing draws near, arriving December 9th on PC. To help prepare for the battles that await you, we’re publishing a series of Devblogs to tell you about some of the features and gameplay elements you can look forward to when you venture deep into the Space Hulk and face the Genestealer menace.

[h1]Solo Campaign[/h1]

Space Hulk: Deathwing features a full solo campaign, with a twisting narrative co-written by renowned Black Library author Gav Thorpe. 

During your journey into the Space Hulk Olethros, you’ll be accompanied by two AI-controlled Terminator squad mates. Brother Barachiel is your Heavy Support, unleashing destruction in battle with weapons such as the Assault Cannon and Plasma Cannon. Brother Nahum is your Apothecary, healing up your squad whenever possible.

[img]https://scontent-cdg2-1.xx.fbcdn.net/t31.0-8/15068980_1123345267741339_2854812183630441147_o.jpg[/img]

You can issue commands to your AI squad mates using a radial menu that can be brought up at any time. Beyond having them follow you on your position, you can also tell them to move to a specific point, guard an area, seal doors, ask Nahum to heal a squad member, and more. 

There are four difficulty modes to choose from in Space Hulk: Deathwing’s solo campaign:
[list][*][b]Disciple[/b] (Easy) – The Emperor protects you from the Xenos.
[*][b]Chapter Champion[/b] (Normal) – You’re used to life on the battlefield.
[*][b]Lion’s Sword[/b] (Hard) – What doesn’t kill us makes us stronger.
[*][b]No Mercy[/b] (Hardest) – To die for the emperor is glorious! [/list]
During the solo campaign, you’ll be playing as a Librarian of the Dark Angels’ Deathwing chapter. This means you have access to a range of Psychic abilities to use in battle, which includes the following: 
[list][*][b]Shockwave[/b] - Releases a flow of energy around the Librarian, pushing back and hurting the enemies in a 360-degree arc.
[*][b]Chain Lightning[/b] - Lightning strikes the first enemy it hits. Turrets and sentries are particularly susceptible to this power.
[*][b]Inferno[/b] - The Librarian draws his powers to create an image of vengeful flame, carbonising all enemies in a line in front of him.
[*][b]Spontaneous combustion[/b] – Causes an enemy to explode, creating a damaging flame blast around them. 
[*][b]Vortex of doom[/b] - The Librarian tears the veil of reality; victims near the vortex are pulverised by the power of the warp.
[*][b]Lion’s Shadow[/b] - The Librarian teleports himself inside an enemy, before exploding out of them.
[*][b]Lion’s Nemesis[/b] - The Librarian uses his mighty powers to become a fearsome Zealot. Just one hit can slay any normal enemy. [/list]
These abilities are unlocked as you progress through the campaign, giving you more options to deal with the Xenos menace! As your squad ventures deeper into Olethros, you’ll also uncover dark secrets, remarkable environments and greater dangers. Of course, going solo isn’t your only option…

[img]https://scontent-cdg2-1.xx.fbcdn.net/t31.0-8/15129626_1123356014406931_8821086735773448570_o.jpg[/img]

[h1]Purging With Friends[/h1]

All missions and chapters are playable in the online co-operative mode. Up to four of the Emperor’s finest can play together at once, with options for joining from the server list, hosting your own game, or automatically finding a suitable game by selecting ‘QuickMatch’.

The server list contains a number of filters to make it easy to find a suitable game. These include options for LAN only, passwords, languages and more. 

From the game lobby screen, players can select from a range of different options to customize their co-operative experience. Hosts can invite their Steam friends directly to the lobby from here. One of four difficulties must be chosen, as well as the option to turn on Friendly Fire. 

It’s possible to play through the chapters in the same order as the solo campaign, or select a single chapter. The host can also construct their own ‘mini campaign’ by putting together a playlist of selected chapters in any order.

[img]https://scontent-cdg2-1.xx.fbcdn.net/t31.0-8/15025469_1123352291073970_1544488590553095775_o.jpg[/img]

Each player is able to select the class they’d like to play from one of the following:
[list][*][b]Librarian[/b] - The only class with access to Psychic powers, including Shockwave and Chain Lightning and Spontaneous Combustion.
[*][b]Apothecary[/b] – Equipped with his Narthecium, the Apothecary can heal his squad mates and activate a heal aura.
[*][b]Assault Speciality[/b] – Unrivalled in melee combat, this Terminator uses hammers, maces and Lightning Claws to rip apart the Xenos hordes.
[*][b]Heavy Weapon Speciality[/b] - Focuses on tearing enemies apart with highly destructive weapons, including the Assault Cannon and Plasma Cannon.
[*][b]Tactical Speciality[/b] – Allows fallen squad mates to return to battle, and has access to a legendary modified Plasma Cannon – the Spear of Caliban. [/list]
Many combinations of classes are possible, though it’s advised to bring a balanced squad that accommodated for each class’ weaknesses for the best chance at survival!

Stay tuned! We’ll soon release more information regarding the exact starting date of the upcoming beta, and how you can gain access.

Pre-order on Steam now and get access to the pre-order Beta, 15% off, and one in-game weapon – the Lost Mace of Corswain: 

http://store.steampowered.com/app/298900/

All glory to the Emperor!

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/45/1478787664-vlcsnap-2015-02-20-12h27m48s65.png[/img]
Greetings Librarians! 

The release of Space Hulk: Deathwing draws near, arriving December 9th on PC. To help prepare for the battles that await you, we’ve written up this Devblog to tell you about some of the features and gameplay elements you can look forward to when you venture deep into the Space Hulk and face the Genestealer menace. 

[b]The Armoury [/b]

Before entering the fray, you will equip yourself (and your AI squad-mates if playing solo) with the best weapons the Imperium has to offer. With a wealth of melee and ranged weaponry combinations available, you might be outnumbered in battle, but you’ll never be outgunned! 

Weapons you’ll be using to purge Genestealers include: 

[list][*][b]Storm Bolter[/b] – Double-barreled version of the classic bolter. Standard issue for the Terminators, each self-propelled bolt explodes with devastating effect after impacting with its target. 
[*][b]Assault Cannon[/b] – Six-barreled, self-loading, and deadly. This fast-firing weapon can deal incredible damage, but is susceptible to jamming during sustained bursts. 
[*][b]Heavy Flamer[/b] – Short-ranged weapon that spews highly volatile streams of flammable liquid that ignites upon contact with air. Particularly destructive against tightly compacted swarms of Xenos.  
[*][b]Plasma Cannon[/b] – Uses plasma technology to unleash superheated matter on its victims. Blasts from the Plasma Cannon can generate the destructive heat of a small sun – earning them the nickname of ‘Sun Guns’ among some of the Imperial populace. This power comes at a cost – the Plasma Cannon can be prone to overheating. 
[*][b]Lightning Claw[/b] – Each Claw is a powered gauntlet, fitted with four Adamantium blades and surrounded by a matter-disrupting power field. Dual-wielded Lightning Claws are capable of carving through armour and flesh with ease. 
[*][b]Thunder Hammer [/b]– This weapon incorporates an energy field generator within its head, triggered to active whenever the Thunder Hammer strikes its target. Upon contact, an incredible amount of force is released, resulting in a blast of energy and a deafeningly roll of thunder.[/list]

Your Armoury will be expanded even further beyond the weapons listed above, as you venture deeper and deeper into the Space Hulk. Each weapon has specific strengths and weaknesses – Librarians wishing to survive the space hulk will need to equip themselves accordingly. 

Librarians are also able to select the Psychic powers they wish to use in battle. Up to three powers may be equipped at once, with each ability activated at the press of a hotkey, and limited by a cooldown. Unlike weaponry, Psychic powers are unlocked through a skill tree. By default, you’ll start with the Shockwave and Chain Lightning powers, with more becoming available as you progress. From forcing back enemies in a 360-degree arc, to purifying Xenos with holy fire, Librarians can adapt to any combat situation!  

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/45/1478787670-vlcsnap-2015-02-20-12h42m20s46.png[/img]

[b]The Genestealers [/b]

Acting as the spearhead for a Hive Fleet, the Genestealers are a species of Tyranid armed with ferocious speed, cunning intellect and large claws that can slash through even the strongest armor. Space Hulk: Deathwing sees you and your squad facing swarms of these Genestealers – but to overcome the Xenos tide, you’ll first need to understand how these devastating foes fight in battle. 

The primary strength of the Genestealers lies in their numbers. A lone Genestealer is no match for the firepower of a Terminator squad. However, if a Xenos swarm is able to fully surround your squad, their powerful claws can make short work of you. 

The Genestealers in Space Hulk: Deathwing can be unpredictable, and will do everything they can do overwhelm you. If a lone Genestealer spots you in the distance, it may run away in order to join a larger ambush later on. Conversely, a large group may split in to two smaller groups, before attacking from all sides. 

When the Genestealers are up-close and personal, it’s a good idea to engage them in melee combat. They may have those claws, but your squad has the finest Force Swords, Lightning Claws and Thunder Hammers in the universe! 

As well as cutting down the Xenos with powerful blows, players can parry their attacks – particularly important when dealing with the larger Genestealer variants. Be warned though, as parrying will not protect your back and sides! 

Positioning is of vital importance in Space Hulk: Deathwing. Forcing Genestealers into a chokepoint is the most efficient way of gunning them down in great numbers under a hail of Storm Bolter fire, or dishing out heavy area-of-effect damage from your psychic powers. Of course, you won’t always be fighting them in tight corridors, and wide open areas are often a convenient place for an unexpected Genestealer ambush… 

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/45/1478787688-vlcsnap-2015-02-20-12h50m52s10.png[/img]

[b]Surviving Olethros [/b]

You and your squad will journey deep into the heart of Olethros, an immense Space Hulk that’s recently emerged from the warp into Imperial space. The Olethros is made up of derelict spaceships, vast asteroids and debris – this mix of different environments means you’ll need to adapt your combat style to take on the Genestealer horde.  

Thankfully, you have a few tactical advantages available. Your auspex scanner, visible in the bottom-right corner of your HUD, is constantly scanning the local area. This gives feedback on the direction of incoming threats, letting you position your squad accordingly. Unfortunately, you won’t be given any idea on the exact numbers or types of enemy you’ll be encountering! 

Much like the tabletop game from which Space Hulk: Deathwing takes its name, the entrances to rooms and corridors are very important. To help stem the tide of Genestealers, you may decide to seal a door shut, slowing down the swarm as the Xenos navigate to an alternate route. 

Occasionally, you’ll come across doors that are already sealed shut. When this happens, you’re presented with an interesting choice: find a different (and slower) path to your objective, or smash down the door, giving the Genestealers another entrance to surround you from. 

Stay tuned for future dev blogs, where we’ll go into more detail about online co-op, more combat details and other exciting features you can expect when Space Hulk: Deathwing releases later this month! 

Pre-order on Steam now and you’ll get access to the pre-order Beta, 15% off, and one in-game weapon – the Lost Mace of Corswain.

http://store.steampowered.com/app/298900

[b]All glory to the Emperor! 

Streum On Studio and Focus Home Interactive[/b]

notes.title: Enter the Space Hulk!

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/44/1478254351-shd-enterthespacehulk-1.gif[/img]

[b]Space Hulk: Deathwing releases December 9![/b]

With only one month left until release, the whole team is working non-stop to add the final layer of polish to our game and deliver the best possible experience to players. We now needs your support: [b]Steam pre-order players are invited to join our upcoming Beta tests.[/b]

Starting next week, we will invite a limited number of pre-order players to join a closed-beta to help us gather the latest technical and gameplay feedback for the game.

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/44/1478254752-spacehulk-deathwing-14.jpg[/img]

[b]Starting around November 20, ALL players who have pre-ordered Space Hulk: Deathwing on Steam will be able to get their first taste through a new beta.[/b]

You'll be able to experience the game's tutorial to learn the basics, before teaming up to complete a mission from the game's campaign with up to 3 other players in co-op! These betas will be the perfect opportunity for us to gather the latest feedback from players, in order to offer the best possible gaming experience at launch.

In the meantime: [b]Enter the Space Hulk and delve deep into its colossal environments to discover their place in the Warhammer 40,000 lore[/b], in our latest trailer!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OhRqPwyHXKg
Each Space Hulk is an amalgamation of ancient ships and space debris, and Olethros is filled with lore from the 10,000 years since the dawn of the Imperium to the 41st Millennium. 

You will be exploring Black Templar ships, troop transports, and even pirate vessels that were lost in the Warp and became part of the Space Hulk OIethros' bowels. We made sure that every inch of the colossal ships, [b]each corridor and each room, contains highly detailed designs, unique architectural styles, and references to Warhammer 40,000 history.[/b]

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/44/1478254569-spacehulk-deathwing-13.jpg[/img]

An incredible amount of care was also given to the enemies and their AI. The Genestealers have many variants with unique abilities and skills, combined with their AI utilizing pack tactics and ambushes that remain faithful to the lore. 

As a Terminator Armour-clad member of the Deathwing, you have access to the most advanced weapons the Imperium has to offer. Available to you and your squad are the iconic Stormbolter and other famous Space Marine weapons and variants. 

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/44/1478254344-shd-enterthespacehulk-2.gif[/img]

notes.title: Watch The Arsenal Trailer!
notes.content:
[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/40/1475483056-mlg-space-hulk.gif[/img]

Greetings Librarians!

[b]Space Hulk: Deathwing showcases some of its big guns in this latest trailer![/b] As the Dark Angels Terminators purify the Space Hulk from the Xeno menace, witness the gunplay of a selection of weapons, the environments and the atmosphere of this upcoming game. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9YmaDbqfO7E

Deathwing Terminators carry some of the biggest and most powerful weapons available to the Imperium. Even the smallest of weapons they employ, the Storm Bolter, is typically a mounted weapon, firing rocket-propelled shells in place of bullets. 

The trailer showcases the deadly assortment of some of the firearms, melee and energy weapons you will wield. The classic Storm Bolter is of course here, alongside Redemption, a unique spread-shot variant capable of ricocheting shots around corners. 

The Heavy Flamer lays fire on walls and floors, cutting off choke points and punishing those who dare cross the line. The Storm Shield can withstand heavy enemy fire, and the Thunder Hammer carries so much latent power that striking it upon either surface and flesh causes an area-of-effect shockwave around the point of impact. 

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/40/1475490031-spacehulk-deathwing-14.jpg[/img]

The labyrinthine Space Hulk that you will explore is dark and dangerous, infested by Xenos. At any time, Genestealers can ambush you, making use of the walls, floorspaces, and ceiling vents. The once-dormant Genestealers have made the Space Hulk their home, and will use every advantage they can get to strike you and your team from your blind spots, and pounce on you from above. True to their swarm-like social structure, they will behave accordingly, and may even fall back to regroup, in order to attack again in greater numbers. 

Don the Terminator power armor, take up your Storm Bolter, and bring glory to the Emperor in Space Hulk: Deathwing when the game launches in November 2016 on PC!

notes.content:
[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/36/1473269231-shd-gif-3.gif[/img]

In this Gamescom trailer, witness the Deathwing squad inspired by the Battle Hymn of Vengeance (written by renowned 40k author Gav Thorpe), hold a last stand against a swarm of insurmountable Genestealers. 

https://youtu.be/PzsDLpNMZq0

Play in coop with friends in a Dark Angels Terminator squad of the elite Deathwing, dispatched to eradicate the Genestealer threat on Space Hulk Olethros, a cluster of derelict ships and debris collected over years of war. 

Playable in single or multiplayer, lead your squad through xeno-infested ships and debris as you search for the source of ominous psychic disturbances. 

[img]http://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2016/36/1473269329-spacehulk-1280x720-parchemin.png[/img]

Your Terminator and your squad can be customized - skills can be learned and levelled up, and you can choose a wide variety of ranged and melee weapons to bring in to the Space Hulk. During battle, command your team to hold choke points, hack into doors, and cover your advance. 

Nothing is as it seems in Space Hulk Olethros, and with a story co-written by acclaimed Dark Angels writer Gavin Thorpe, you can be sure that easter eggs are hidden around every corner. 

[b]Don the Terminator power armor and bring glory to the Emperor in Space Hulk: Deathwing when the game launches in November 2016 on PC![/b]
